title: 分散システム
subtitle: Distributed Object Oriented Systems
educationalGoal: A distributed system is a technology for integrating both computers and networks, and is an attempt to link computers that originally operated independently to a network. In this class, we will focus on computer architecture, processes, client-server, communication, naming, clock and synchronization, fault-tolerance, and security, which are necessary for learning distributed systems.
advice: Before each class session, students are required to review the prerequisite content and complete a series of questions to confirm that they have mastered the content before attending that week's lectures. The students are required to attend the lectures of the week. In each class session, the main focus is on solving application problems in class based on the assumption that the students understand the pre-study contents. The main focus of each class session is to solve application problems in class, assuming that the students understand the prior learning content. The course is not designed to be an achievement test, as is conventionally the case, in which a lecture is given from a textbook and later students are asked to reproduce parts of the lecture in a written test. The course does not use a test to check the level of achievement of students.
books: Distributed System (in Japanese) Distributed System (in English)
requiredKnowledge: The units of “Programming 3” and “Information Network” are expected to have been acquired. Attendance is completely unrelated to student evaluations. However, if students do not attend at least two-thirds of the whole course, they will not be eligible to take the achievement confirmation test. Instead of covering all the contents described in the textbooks, we will select and explain as necessary. Then, after each commentary, students will have group work to solve presented problems and will give a presentation at the beginning of the next class.

achievementLevels.ideal: Within 15 weeks you will be able to 1. Analyze the technical advantages of specific developments in distributed computer systems. 2. Demonstrate system analysis using existing scientific and engineering knowledge. 3. Further develop an attitude that allows them to explain problems clearly. Improve the quality of feedback. 4. Clearly summarize the analysis in a presentation or report. 5. Evaluate the demonstrated analysis of others.
achievementLevels.standard: Within 15 weeks you will be able to 1. Explain the technical advantages in the field of distributed systems. 2. Explain how to analyze a system using existing scientific and engineering knowledge. 3. Be able to clearly explain the problem. 4. Be able to summarize the analysis in a presentation or report. 5. Be able to understand the demonstrated analysis of others.

lessons.content: 1. Overview of distributed systems I will take up what a distributed system is and explain some of its advantages over a centralized system.
2. Types of distributed systems Understand the types and purposes of distributed systems. Learn what is different about how each type of configuration.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 2 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 3 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 3. Communication Learn about basic reference models and basic functions for exchanging data between components of a distributed system.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 3 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 4 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 4. Naming Explain common naming issues in distributed systems and learn about the main methods of naming.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 4 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 5 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 5. Architecture Learn basic design and concepts such as the design philosophy and basic design of distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 5 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 6 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 6. Process Learn about the execution units in a distributed system such as “process” and “thread”.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 6 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 7 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 7. Client-Server model Learn the classification and characteristics of both clients and servers from several perspectives.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 7 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 8 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 8. Clock and Synchronization Learn about the basic methods of clock synchronization and the exclusive control algorithms in distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 8 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 9 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 9. Fault Torrent Learn about basic concepts and techniques for introducing fault tolerance into distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 9 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 10 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 10. Network Security Learn about cryptographic technologies, authentication technologies, communication methods, and access control.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 10 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 11 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 11. Distributed files and objects Learn the advantages and disadvantages of distributed files compared to centralized file systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 11 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 12 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 12. Distributed web systems Learn about the characteristics of distributed web systems for processing a great deal of data.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 12 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 13 of the textbook)

lessons.content: Hold a lecture on distributed systems with external lecturers.
